rules.title: California AB 325: common pricing algorithm prohibition (Bus. & Prof. Code 16729)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade, or to use or distribute one while coercing another person to adopt its recommended price or commercial term. The text never mentions rent, housing, landlords, tenants or leases; applying it to rental housing is an inference, not a statement.

needs_fact: rental_housing_applicability: AB 325 amends the Cartwright Act and its text has no mention of rent, housing, landlord, tenant or lease
prohibition bites only when used as part of a contract, combination or conspiracy, or with coercion
coverage_conditions.note: Scope to rental housing is inferred, not stated; the prohibition is conditional, so it is not a flat ban on every California rental address.

rules.exemptions: Section 16729(c): nothing in the section impairs or limits the applicability of antitrust laws.
rules.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code sec. 16729 (added by Stats. 2025, ch. 338 (AB 325))
rules.quoted_span: (a) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.

supporting_spans.text: CHAPTER 338 An act to add Sections 16729 and 16756.1 to the Business and Professions Code
Approved by Governor October 06, 2025. Filed with Secretary of State October 06, 2025.

(c) Nothing in this section shall impair or limit the applicability of antitrust laws.
